Thanks! I solved it. 
Now I have another problem. When I ran the prediction data I received an issue. I'm using the toturial of Paula Moragada: https://www.paulamoraga.com/tutorial-geostatistical-data/#1_data
This is the code:

## Data
zoo <- read.csv("./isoscapebase_final_ALL.csv",fileEncoding = "Latin1", check.names = F)
#subset of zooplakton
d <- zoo %>%
  group_by(FG, Sector, X, Y, d13CcorrSu,profgebco) %>%
  filter(FG=="ZP")

library(sp)
library(rgdal)
zoo_sps  <- SpatialPoints(d[, c("X", "Y")], proj4string = CRS("+proj=utm +zone=18"))
zoo_spst <- spTransform(zoo_sps, CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84"))

d[, c("long", "lat")] <- coordinates(zoo_pts)

###2.4 Environmental covariates
Depth_ras<-raster("C:/Users/dodin/Desktop/Proyectos Isoscapes/INLA/paperLu_sami_try/gebco_2022_n-52.0_s-69.0_w-70.0_e-54.0.tif")

# extract data for each sample location
env_data_pts <- extract(Depth_ras, zoo_pts)
#3.2 Build mesh
library(INLA)
coo <- cbind(d$long, d$lat)
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = coo, max.edge = c(1, 5), cutoff = 0.01)
mesh$n
plot(mesh)
points(coo, col = "red")
#3.3 Build the SPDE model on the mesh
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh, alpha = 2)
#3.4 Index set
indexs <- inla.spde.make.index("s", spde$n.spde)
lengths(indexs)
#3.5 Projector matrix
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coo)
#3.6 Prediction data

dp <- rasterToPoints(Depth_ras)
dim(dp)
ra <- aggregate(Depth_ras, fact = 5, fun = mean)
dp <- rasterToPoints(ra)
dim(dp)
coop <- dp[, c("long", "lat")]
Error in dp[, c("long", "lat")] : subscript out of bounds

I can't find the mistake. Does any one can help me?
